turns.prompt_text: I would like to visit a scrap yard. I'm not sure what exactly I would find. I imagine it's different for different places but I would like to see what's around there
turns.response_html:
Visiting a scrap or salvage yard is a unique experience, and what you will find depends entirely on the type of facility you visit. Generally, yards fall into a few distinct categories, ranging from industrial metal recycling to self-service automotive goldmines.

What You Typically Find at Different Yards

  • Scrap Metal Processors: These facilities focus on raw material recycling. You won't find organized parts here; instead, you will see massive piles of sorted ferrous metals (iron, steel) and non-ferrous metals (copper tubing, brass fixtures, aluminum wiring). They also process large household appliances (refrigerators, stoves) and commercial e-scrap.
  • Full-Service Auto Salvage Yards: These yards handle cars, trucks, and SUVs. In a full-service setup, the yard staff inventories the vehicles, removes the high-demand components, and catalogs them. When you visit, you usually interact with a front counter to buy pre-pulled, tested parts rather than wandering the rows of vehicles yourself.
  • Self-Service "Pull-Your-Own" Yards: This is the classic "junkyard" experience. Rows of vehicles—often hundreds of them—are propped up on wheel stands. You bring your own toolbox, sign a waiver, pay a small gate fee, and physically hunt down and remove the exact mechanical components, trim pieces, or hardware adapters you need.

Here are some options located right in the area depending on the style of yard you want to explore:

Jerry Carney & Sons, Inc.

Jerry Carney & Sons, Inc. is a long-standing, structured automotive recycling facility located on the southeast side of town. They specialize in high-quality used and replacement auto parts for cars, light trucks, and SUVs.

  • The Setup: This is primarily a full-service, organized facility. They buy late-model damaged and older vehicles, catalog the inventory, and dismantle components for systematic recycling.
  • What to Expect: Rather than roaming a chaotic field, you will find a professional office team that can look up exact parts availability in their database. It is highly recommended to call ahead to see if they have the specific model components you are curious about.

Mike Louis Body, Paint, Towing, Sandblasting, Mechanical and Salvage

Mike Louis Body, Paint, Towing, Sandblasting, Mechanical and Salvage operates an all-in-one automotive service center on East Lincoln Way that includes a smaller, dedicated salvage yard operation alongside their body shop and towing services.

  • The Setup: Because they operate a diverse mechanical and restoration business, their scrap and salvage operation is more tightly integrated with local vehicle recovery.
  • What to Expect: They focus heavily on buying junk cars, scrap metal, and catalytic converters. It is a smaller-scale commercial operation compared to massive dedicated auto lots, offering a glimpse into how a local garage manages vehicle recycling and vintage restoration materials.

Wrench' N Go

Wrench' N Go is the region's dedicated self-service salvage yard, located just south of downtown Des Moines. If you want the hands-on experience of wandering rows of old machinery with a toolkit, this is where you want to go.

  • The Setup: They host an ever-changing inventory of over 900 vehicles set up on wheel stands and organized so visitors can safely strip parts.
  • What to Expect: You must be 18 or older to enter the yard. You bring your own tools, pay a tiny entry fee, and can use their customer interchange system to find out which vehicles share the mechanical components or hardware systems you are trying to understand or harvest.

Are you looking for a specific mechanical part or materials for a project, or are you just looking to drop off some old equipment?
